passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD told Moses to go to Pharaoh.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Pharaoh.
The LORD said, “Let My people go.”
The LORD said, “Let them go so they may worship Me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃

passages.text: But if you continue to restrain them and refuse to let them go, then the hand of the LORD will bring a severe plague on your livestock in the field—on your horses, donkeys, camels, herds, and flocks.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh holds the Israelites in slavery.
The LORD speaks to Pharaoh through Moses.
The LORD gives Pharaoh a warning.
If you refuse to let the Israelites go,
If you keep holding them back,
Then the LORD will act against you.
The LORD will strike your livestock in the field.
Your horses will be struck.
Your donkeys will be struck.
Your camels will be struck.
Your cattle will be struck.
Your sheep and goats will be struck.
A very severe plague will come on them.
This plague will come from the LORD.
passages.original: כִּ֛י אִם־ מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֑חַ וְעוֹדְךָ֖ מַחֲזִ֥יק בָּֽם׃ הִנֵּ֨ה יַד־ יְהוָ֜ה הוֹיָ֗ה בְּמִקְנְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּסּוּסִ֤ים בַּֽחֲמֹרִים֙ בַּגְּמַלִּ֔ים בַּבָּקָ֖ר וּבַצֹּ֑אן דֶּ֖בֶר כָּבֵ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: But the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD will act with power.
The LORD will make a clear difference between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt.
The LORD will protect the animals that belong to the Israelites.
No animal belonging to the Israelites will die.
The animals of Egypt will not have this protection.
passages.original: וְהִפְלָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין מִקְנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבֵ֖ין מִקְנֵ֣ה מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹ֥א יָמ֛וּת מִכָּל־ לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: The LORD set a time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD set a specific time.
The LORD said, “Tomorrow I will act.”
The LORD said, “I will do this thing in the land.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֥שֶׂם יְהוָ֖ה מוֹעֵ֣ד לֵאמֹ֑ר מָחָ֗ר יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And the next day the LORD did just that. All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted the next day.
The LORD did what He said He would do.
All the livestock of the Egyptians died.
None of the livestock of the Israelites died.
Not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיָּ֕מָת כֹּ֖ל מִקְנֵ֣ה מִצְרָ֑יִם וּמִמִּקְנֵ֥ה בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹא־ מֵ֥ת אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: Pharaoh sent officials and found that none of the livestock of the Israelites had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh sent his officials to investigate.
They checked the livestock of the Israelites.
They found that not one animal belonging to the Israelites had died.
Pharaoh’s heart became hard.
Pharaoh refused to let the people of Israel go.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֗ה לֹא־ מֵ֛ת מִמִּקְנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־ אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּכְבַּד֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take handfuls of soot from the furnace; in the sight of Pharaoh, Moses is to toss it into the air.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD gave them a command.
He told them to take handfuls of soot from the furnace.
Moses must throw the soot into the air.
He must do this while Pharaoh is watching.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹן֒ קְח֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מְלֹ֣א חָפְנֵיכֶ֔ם פִּ֖יחַ כִּבְשָׁ֑ן וּזְרָק֥וֹ מֹשֶׁ֛ה הַשָּׁמַ֖יְמָה לְעֵינֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and festering boils will break out on man and beast throughout the land.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses and Aaron.
God gave them a command.
God told them to take soot from a furnace.
God said Moses must throw the soot into the air.
The soot will become fine dust.
The dust will spread over all the land of Egypt.
The dust will fall on people and animals.
Painful boils will appear on people in Egypt.
Painful boils will appear on animals in Egypt.
Boils will cover all the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה לְאָבָ֔ק עַ֖ל כָּל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהָיָ֨ה עַל־ הָאָדָ֜ם וְעַל־ הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה לִשְׁחִ֥ין פֹּרֵ֛חַ אֲבַעְבֻּעֹ֖ת בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So they took soot from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses tossed it into the air, and festering boils broke out on man and beast.
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron took soot from the furnace.
They stood before Pharaoh.
Moses threw the soot into the air.
Boils broke out on people.
Boils broke out on animals.
The boils were painful and had sores.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֞וּ אֶת־ פִּ֣יחַ הַכִּבְשָׁ֗ן וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיִּזְרֹ֥ק אֹת֛וֹ מֹשֶׁ֖ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יְמָה וַיְהִ֗י שְׁחִין֙ אֲבַעְבֻּעֹ֔ת פֹּרֵ֕חַ בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: The magicians could not stand before Moses, because the boils had broken out on them and on all the Egyptians.
passages.sermon:
The magicians served Pharaoh in Egypt.
Boils broke out on the magicians.
Boils also broke out on all the Egyptians.
The magicians could not stand before Moses.
The boils caused their suffering.
The boils made them unable to stand before Moses.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ יָכְל֣וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֗ים לַעֲמֹ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה מִפְּנֵ֣י הַשְּׁחִ֑ין כִּֽי־ הָיָ֣ה הַשְּׁחִ֔ין בַּֽחֲרְטֻמִּ֖ם וּבְכָל־ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said to Moses.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD made Pharaoh’s heart stubborn.
Pharaoh refused to listen to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD had already told Moses this would happen.
passages.original: וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD told Moses to get up early in the morning.
The LORD told Moses to stand before Pharaoh.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Pharaoh.
The LORD told Moses to say, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says.”
The LORD said, “Let My people go.”
The LORD said, “Let them go so that they may worship Me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃

passages.text: Otherwise, I will send all My plagues against you and your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD speaks to Pharaoh.
The LORD says, “I will send all My plagues against you.
I will send My plagues against your officials.
I will send My plagues against your people.
I do this so you may know something important.
There is no one like Me in all the earth.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֗את אֲנִ֨י שֹׁלֵ֜חַ אֶת־ כָּל־ מַגֵּפֹתַי֙ אֶֽל־ לִבְּךָ֔ וּבַעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וּבְעַמֶּ֑ךָ בַּעֲב֣וּר תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין כָּמֹ֖נִי בְּכָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: For by this time I could have stretched out My hand and struck you and your people with a plague to wipe you off the earth.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD speaks to Pharaoh through Moses.
The LORD has great power over all the earth.
The LORD says, “By now I could have stretched out My hand.
I could have struck you with a plague.
I could have struck your people with a plague.
You and your people would have been wiped off the earth.”
passages.original: כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֶת־ יָדִ֔י וָאַ֥ךְ אוֹתְךָ֛ וְאֶֽת־ עַמְּךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑בֶר וַתִּכָּחֵ֖ד מִן־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power to you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
God said, “I have raised you up for a reason.
I want to show you My power.
I want everyone in the world to hear My name.
I want people everywhere to know who I am.”
passages.original: וְאוּלָ֗ם בַּעֲב֥וּר זֹאת֙ הֶעֱמַדְתִּ֔יךָ בַּעֲב֖וּר הַרְאֹתְךָ֣ אֶת־ כֹּחִ֑י וּלְמַ֛עַן סַפֵּ֥ר שְׁמִ֖י בְּכָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Still, you lord it over My people and do not allow them to go.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh acts with pride and power over the Israelites.
Pharaoh continues to oppress My people, the Israelites.
Pharaoh refuses to let the Israelites go free.
passages.original: עוֹדְךָ֖ מִסְתּוֹלֵ֣ל בְּעַמִּ֑י לְבִלְתִּ֖י שַׁלְּחָֽם׃

passages.text: Behold, at this time tomorrow I will rain down the worst hail that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded until now.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Pharaoh through Moses.
God said, “I will act tomorrow at this time.
I will send hail on Egypt.
This hail will be very heavy.
No hail like this has ever fallen in Egypt.
This will be true from the day Egypt began until now.”
passages.original: הִנְנִ֤י מַמְטִיר֙ כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֔ר בָּרָ֖ד כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־ הָיָ֤ה כָמֹ֙הוּ֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם לְמִן־ הַיּ֥וֹם הִוָּסְדָ֖ה וְעַד־ עָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: So give orders now to shelter your livestock and everything you have in the field. Every man or beast that remains in the field and is not brought inside will die when the hail comes down upon them.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Pharaoh through Moses.
God warned Pharaoh about a coming disaster.
God said, “Send word now.
Bring your livestock into shelter.
Bring everything you have in the field into shelter.
Any person who stays in the field will be in danger.
Any animal that stays in the field will be in danger.
If they are not brought inside, they will die.
Hail will fall on them and they will die.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁלַ֤ח הָעֵז֙ אֶֽת־ מִקְנְךָ֔ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְךָ֖ בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה כָּל־ הָאָדָ֨ם וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִמָּצֵ֣א בַשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְלֹ֤א יֵֽאָסֵף֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וְיָרַ֧ד עֲלֵהֶ֛ם הַבָּרָ֖ד וָמֵֽתוּ׃

passages.text: Those among Pharaoh’s officials who feared the word of the LORD hurried to bring their servants and livestock to shelter, but those who disregarded the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
The LORD warned of deadly hail coming to Egypt.
Some of Pharaoh’s officials heard the LORD’s warning.
These officials feared the word of the LORD.
They quickly brought their servants into the houses.
They also brought their livestock into the houses.
Other officials did not care about the LORD’s warning.
They left their servants in the field.
They left their livestock in the field.
passages.original: הַיָּרֵא֙ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מֵֽעַבְדֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֑ה הֵנִ֛יס אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֥יו וְאֶת־ מִקְנֵ֖הוּ אֶל־ הַבָּתִּֽים׃ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ שָׂ֛ם לִבּ֖וֹ אֶל־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֥יו וְאֶת־ מִקְנֵ֖הוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that hail may fall on all the land of Egypt—on man and beast and every plant of the field throughout the land of Egypt.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to stretch out his hand toward heaven.
The LORD wanted hail to fall on the land of Egypt.
The hail would fall everywhere in Egypt.
The hail would fall on people in Egypt.
The hail would fall on animals in Egypt.
The hail would fall on every plant in the fields of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה נְטֵ֤ה אֶת־ יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וִיהִ֥י בָרָ֖ד בְּכָל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־ הָאָדָ֣ם וְעַל־ הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וְעַ֛ל כָּל־ עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So Moses stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning struck the earth. So the LORD rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet of God.
Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD sent thunder.
The LORD sent hail.
Lightning struck the ground.
The LORD caused hail to fall on the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨ט מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶת־ מַטֵּהוּ֮ עַל־ הַשָּׁמַיִם֒ וַֽיהוָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן קֹלֹת֙ וּבָרָ֔ד וַתִּ֥הֲלַךְ אֵ֖שׁ אָ֑רְצָה וַיַּמְטֵ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בָּרָ֖ד עַל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The hail fell and the lightning continued flashing through it. The hail was so severe that nothing like it had ever been seen in all the land of Egypt from the time it became a nation.
passages.sermon:
God sent a plague on Egypt.
Hail fell on the land of Egypt.
Fire flashed inside the hail.
The hail was very heavy.
No one had ever seen hail like this in Egypt before.
This was true from the time Egypt became a nation.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בָרָ֔ד וְאֵ֕שׁ מִתְלַקַּ֖חַת בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבָּרָ֑ד כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ הָיָ֤ה כָמֹ֙הוּ֙ בְּכָל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵאָ֖ז הָיְתָ֥ה לְגֽוֹי׃

passages.text: Throughout the land of Egypt, the hail struck down everything in the field, both man and beast; it beat down every plant of the field and stripped every tree.
passages.sermon:
God sent a plague of hail on Egypt.
The hail fell everywhere in the land of Egypt.
The hail struck everything that was in the field.
The hail struck people who were in the field.
The hail struck animals who were in the field.
The hail beat down every plant in the field.
The hail broke every tree in the field.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨ךְ הַבָּרָ֜ד בְּכָל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם אֵ֚ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה מֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־ בְּהֵמָ֑ה וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ עֵ֤שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה֙ הִכָּ֣ה הַבָּרָ֔ד וְאֶת־ כָּל־ עֵ֥ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה שִׁבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: The only place where it did not hail was in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived.
passages.sermon:
The land of Goshen was a region in Egypt.
The Israelites lived in Goshen.
Hail did not fall in Goshen.
Everywhere else in Egypt, hail fell.
Only Goshen was spared from the hail.
passages.original: רַ֚ק בְּאֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֔שֶׁן אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֥א הָיָ֖ה בָּרָֽד׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he said. “The LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh called them to come to him.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh said, “I have sinned this time.”
Pharaoh said, “The LORD is righteous.”
Pharaoh said, “I and my people are wicked.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח פַּרְעֹ֗ה וַיִּקְרָא֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֖ם חָטָ֣אתִי הַפָּ֑עַם יְהוָה֙ הַצַּדִּ֔יק וַאֲנִ֥י וְעַמִּ֖י הָרְשָׁעִֽים׃

passages.text: Pray to the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail. I will let you go; you do not need to stay any longer.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh asked them to pray to the LORD.
Pharaoh said there had been enough thunder from God.
Pharaoh said there had been enough hail from God.
Pharaoh promised to let the Israelites go.
Pharaoh said the Israelites did not need to stay any longer.
passages.original: הַעְתִּ֙ירוּ֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וְרַ֕ב מִֽהְיֹ֛ת קֹלֹ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים וּבָרָ֑ד וַאֲשַׁלְּחָ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תֹסִפ֖וּן לַעֲמֹֽד׃

passages.text: Moses said to him, “When I have left the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth is the LORD’s.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Moses said, “When I leave the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The thunder will stop.
There will be no more hail.
This will happen so you will know that the earth belongs to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּצֵאתִי֙ אֶת־ הָעִ֔יר אֶפְרֹ֥שׂ אֶת־ כַּפַּ֖י אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה הַקֹּל֣וֹת יֶחְדָּל֗וּן וְהַבָּרָד֙ לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־ ע֔וֹד לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֥י לַיהוָ֖ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: But as for you and your officials, I know that you still do not fear the LORD our God.”
passages.sermon: Moses spoke to Pharaoh and his officials.\r\nMoses said, “I know something about you and your officials.\r\nYou and your officials do not fear the LORD our God yet.”
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֖ה וַעֲבָדֶ֑יךָ יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֚י טֶ֣רֶם תִּֽירְא֔וּן מִפְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: (Now the flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley was ripe and the flax was in bloom; but the wheat and spelt were not destroyed, because they are late crops.)
passages.sermon:
The flax and the barley were destroyed.
The barley was ripe.
The flax was in bloom.
The wheat was not destroyed.
The spelt was not destroyed.
The wheat and the spelt are late crops.
passages.original: וְהַפִּשְׁתָּ֥ה וְהַשְּׂעֹרָ֖ה נֻכָּ֑תָה כִּ֤י הַשְּׂעֹרָה֙ אָבִ֔יב וְהַפִּשְׁתָּ֖ה גִּבְעֹֽל׃ וְהַחִטָּ֥ה וְהַכֻּסֶּ֖מֶת לֹ֣א נֻכּ֑וּ כִּ֥י אֲפִילֹ֖ת הֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Then Moses departed from Pharaoh, went out of the city, and spread out his hands to the LORD. The thunder and hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of the Israelites.
Moses left Pharaoh.
Moses went out of the city.
Moses spread out his hands to the LORD.
The thunder stopped.
The hail stopped.
The rain no longer fell on the land.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה מֵעִ֤ם פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־ הָעִ֔יר וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחְדְּל֤וּ הַקֹּלוֹת֙ וְהַבָּרָ֔ד וּמָטָ֖ר לֹא־ נִתַּ֥ךְ אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had ceased, he sinned again and hardened his heart—he and his officials.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh saw that the rain had stopped.
He saw that the hail had stopped.
He saw that the thunder had stopped.
Pharaoh sinned again.
He made his heart stubborn.
His officials also made their hearts stubborn.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא פַּרְעֹ֗ה כִּֽי־ חָדַ֨ל הַמָּטָ֧ר וְהַבָּרָ֛ד וְהַקֹּלֹ֖ת וַיֹּ֣סֶף לַחֲטֹ֑א וַיַּכְבֵּ֥ד לִבּ֖וֹ ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh’s heart became hard.
Pharaoh refused to let the Israelites go.
The LORD had spoken this through Moses.
The LORD said Pharaoh would not let the Israelites go.
Pharaoh acted just as the LORD had said.
passages.original: וַֽיֶּחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
